text:
jordana: Hey team, newbie question. I'm prototyping an embeddings-heavy demo from my laptop and I'm using an ephemeral token issued via SSO (Okta). After ~10-15m the token either starts returning 429s or the requests fail entirely. Is there a difference in quotas between ephemeral/SSO tokens and regular hosted keys? Who do I ping for a short demo quota bump for embeddings, and are there recommended settings (batching, rate limits) to avoid this during a live demo?
onboard-bot: Welcome to Redwood! :tada: New hires with quick quota/demo asks often DM devops or post here. See the onboarding doc: https://redwood.dev/onboarding and the demo request form: https://internal.redwood.com/demo-bump (internal).
platform-eng: Short answers: 1) ephemeral tokens are short TTL by default (15m) and require refresh; they share the org's hosted quota but we also enforce per-token and per-ip buckets. 2) Embeddings are metered differently (units per vector) and high QPS can hit throughput caps faster than simple completions. For demos, ask for a temporary demo key or an extended ephemeral TTL. For production you should use Vault/ephemeral refresh flow.
devops: We can provision a 24h or 72h demo key (hosted or sandbox) depending on needs. To request a hosted bump include expected QPS, model (e.g., rwd-embed-1), vector size, and demo window. If you want a low-friction option right now we can issue a sandbox key with separate quota.
sam: Please paste the raw response headers (redact any secrets). Look for `x-rate-limit-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-reset`, `x-request-id`, and whether the error is 401 vs 429. 401 indicates TTL/refresh problems; 429 indicates quota. Also add the curl you used so we can see if the client is retrying or if there's aggressive parallelism. Example troubleshooting curl: ```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ephemeral-REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","input":["a","b"]}' -v
```
jordana: here's a sanitized snippet from the failing run (no key pasted):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: req_aa11bb22
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1759877000
content-type: application/json

Body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"token exceeded request quota"}
I saw this after about 12 minutes of continual test runs at ~20 req/s (small batches).
billing: Note that embeddings cost and quota are treated as separate units; sandbox/demo keys often have an independent quota bucket but not infinite credits. If you need a larger demo allocation for customer-facing work, include expected token/embedding units in your request so Billing/Growth can provision trial credits.
sre-ops: If you see token failures after ~15m specifically, verify whether the token is expiring (401) vs being throttled (429). For TTL issues: ephemeral tokens issued via SSO sometimes require a refresh call; our CLI has a `redwood auth refresh` helper. For pure 429s: reduce concurrency, increase batch size (send more inputs per embeddings call), and add exponential backoff with jitter.
jordana: Is there a recommended batch size for embeddings to reduce QPS? My prototype currently sends single-input requests because it's simpler.
platform-eng: For many embedding workloads batching 8-64 inputs per request is typical. Bigger batches amortize overhead and reduce per-call rate. Watch memory on the client and latency goals; larger batches increase latency but reduce QPS. Also consider async batching in your demo harness.
devops: To get an immediate unblock we can: 1) issue a 24h sandbox key (separate embeddings quota) 2) extend ephemeral TTL for a specific demo session 3) grant a temporary hosted bump. DM me the demo window and expected vector-units and we'll pick the least-friction option.
sam: Also instrument the client to emit `x-request-id` on failures and paste it here when you hit 429s — we can trace the request through the gateway and see whether per-ip or per-token limits fired.
jordana: Thanks, everyone. I'll change to batched calls, add backoff, try the sandbox option, and DM devops with the demo dates + expected QPS. Appreciate the quick help! :thumbsup:
